abstract: Mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1 (mTORC1) regulates diverse cellular processes through its kinase activity and is essential for nervous system development. Although mTORC1 hyperactivation causes numerous neurodevelopmental disorders, its downstream targets in the developing nervous system remain poorly defined. Here, by profiling thousands of proteins and tens of thousands of phosphosites during the neurogenic phase in mouse and human models, we systematically define the proteomic and phosphoproteomic landscape downstream of mTORC1 during neurodevelopment. To facilitate community access, we developed PhosphoTargets, an interactive platform comprising protein and phosphoprotein expression data from mTORC1 models and patient tissue. We demonstrate the utility of this resource by identifying the deubiquitylating enzyme USP9X as a novel mTORC1 substrate and showing that mTORC1-dependent phosphorylation of USP9X regulates human neural progenitor cell proliferation. Furthermore, integration with gene expression datasets reveals a new role for mTORC1 in the regulation of mRNA splicing. Together, these data provide a comprehensive resource for investigating mTORC1 signalling mechanisms and reveal novel processes through which mTORC1 regulates neurodevelopment.
